user_request: Agree on propose plan continue when the machine is less used and some items complete
approved_items: N1, N2, N4 and the N3 literature check (N5 deferred until N1)
start_rule: N3 literature check starts immediately (no compute). N1, N2 and N4 start when A1 and A2 (proposal 2) have reported, so their heavy builds are not overloaded.
method: Elenchus tiers A/L/C/X; ledger + gate per paper; positive + negative controls; producer != verifier (independent Opus audit); publish per paper after audit (not REJECT), revision applied, Lean controls caught, a result remains (negative results count).

items.title: Zero-point classification theorem for Gaussian potentials: the triangular lattice is a local minimizer of the harmonic zero-point energy iff a is outside (a-, a+)
statements: N1a: rigorous enclosures of the two roots a- ~ 0.377 and a+ ~ 1.581 of the zero-point curvature at the triangular point (interval arithmetic in a).

N1b: certified sign of the curvature (or of B2's majorant bound) on whole a-intervals covering (a-+eps, a+-eps) (not a local minimum) and on compact intervals outside [a-, a+] (strict local minimum, needs a two-sided certified positive curvature plus the C2/critical-point hypotheses).
N1c: Lean assembly as in B2 (logic + rational certificates kernel-checked; ball arithmetic and glue tiered C).
items.kill: if the enclosures cannot separate the roots or a sign on an interval, report the best certified sub-intervals

items.title: No zero-point universal optimality for physical potentials: certified 'triangular is not a local minimum of E_zp' for Yukawa (kappa 1, 2), dipolar exciton (d 0.1, 0.5) and Riesz s = 3, 4
statements: N2: for each potential refuted numerically in P2, extend B2's linear-response majorant certificate (with rigorous lattice-sum tails for algebraic decay) to certify E_zp(L_t) < E_zp(L_rho) for small shears; negative control: a potential where P2 found triangular a local minimum (e.g. Riesz s = 6 or Gaussian a = 2) must not certify.
items.kill: report per potential; slowly decaying tails (Riesz 3, dipolar) may defeat the certificate: report the obstacle

items.title: Literature check before any attempt: best known lower bounds on the 3D jellium (Wigner) energy and their relation to the Lieb-Oxford constant; is a certified improvement beyond Lieb-Narnhofer (-1.4508) still open and meaningful?
statements: N3: a verified literature map (alphaXiv, primary sources): current best rigorous lower bound for 3D jellium energy per particle, the best Lieb-Oxford constant bounds, and whether improving the jellium bound would improve them; go / no-go with reasons.
items.kill: no-go if the best known bound already exceeds what B3's residual plan could certify

items.title: Isothermal theorem of evolutionary graph theory (Lieberman-Hauert-Nowak 2005) in Lean: on isothermal (weight-balanced) graphs the fixation probability equals the Moran value
statements: N4: define the Moran process on a weighted directed graph; prove that if the graph is isothermal (all temperatures equal / circulation) the number of mutants is a birth-death chain with the Moran ratio r, hence fixation probability (1 - r^-1)/(1 - r^-N) for a single random mutant, reusing P7's kernel-checked Moran fixation; negative control: a star graph (an amplifier) differs on an explicit instance.
items.kill: two budgets; report partial (e.g. the embedded birth-death reduction only)
